div.note: Latin only (Quadripartitus, after III Atr, Pax and Wal; from R, compared with TMHkBr). Heading only in R; ‘Lundonie’ probably stood in the archetype, perhaps in the heading or prologue of the lost Old English original. Dated c. 991–c. 1002.; F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads), October 2026 (was “c.991–c.1002; ?mid-990's (Wormald)”, now “c.991–c.1002 (Liebermann); ?mid-990s (Wormald)”); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date at the head of the text); Wormald, Making of English Law I; Whitelock, English Historical Documents I, October 2026 (was “c.991–c.1002 (Liebermann); ?mid-990s (Wormald)”, now “c.991–c.1002 (Liebermann, I p. 232); ?mid-990s (Wormald, MEL p. 443)”); BQ: page of each of Liebermann’s texts and of his German, checked against Liebermann, Gesetze I (our double-read transcription), October 2026 (e.g. was “(empty)”, now “Q 232; German 233”; 38 rows of IV Atr); V: page of the modern editor’s text / translation, checked against Robertson (translation on the facing page), October 2026 (e.g. was “70”, now “70 / 71”; 38 rows of IV Atr)

so R; no heading T [Lundonie stood (according to the preceding note XX. De i. Lundonie) in the archetype, and so perhaps in the heading or prologue of the Anglo-Saxon original]

Eine Insc. fand sich wohl im Q-Archetyp und enthielt das Wort ‘Lundon’, das Q ebensogut in seiner Agsächs. Vorlage gelesen wie aus dem Text 1—2, 5 kombiniert haben kann. Im Agsächs. Texte war es vielleicht das Überbleibsel eines jedenfalls einst dagewesenen Prologs. Vgl. Gl London 13—18a

An Insc. was probably present in the Q archetype and contained the word ‘Lundon’, which Q may just as well have read in his Anglo-Saxon exemplar as have put together from the text of 1—2, 5. In the Anglo-Saxon text it was perhaps the remnant of a prologue that had at any rate once existed. Cf. Gl London 13—18a
